reply_text:
I found the quoted words on the page exactly. My reading is **pass**: the claim meets all four parts of the rule, and it is not one of his recorded claims.

**Page check.** The page opened. It is a LessWrong post by WilliamKiely, dated 7 April 2022, that transcribes excerpts from DeepMind: The Podcast. It dates Episode 9 to 15 March 2022. At 7:11, after Hannah Fry asks "If you're a betting man, then when do you think that will be?", Hassabis says: "So I think that the progress so far has been pretty phenomenal. I think that [AGI] it's coming relatively soon in the next you know–I wouldn't be super surprised–in the next decade or two." That matches the candidate exactly; the "[AGI]" in brackets is the transcriber's own addition. The post is a listener's partial transcript that links each quote to its time in the YouTube recording. It is not a news report, so I am not marking it coverage only. Whoever checks this may still want to listen to the recording at 7:11 to confirm the transcription.

**The four parts of the rule:**
1. **Role:** In March 2022 Hassabis was chief executive of DeepMind, a company that builds frontier AI models. That qualifies.
2. **Forward-looking and about AI:** He says AGI is coming. "I wouldn't be super surprised" is a hedge, not a probability, so the claim is scored as said. It is not framed as a hypothetical.
3. **Date or length of time:** "The next decade or two" is a range of spans counted from the day he said it. Under the due-year rule the later end applies, so it is due in 2042. It is not "a few years" or "as little as X", so the rule's reading 3 (those count as undated) does not apply.
4. **Primary source:** A verbatim transcript tied to the recording counts.

**Already recorded?** No. None of his recorded files is from 2022. The nearest are the 2011 "twenty-plus years" claim, the 2023-07-10 "next decade" claim and the 2024-02-23 twenty-year-plan claim. They have different dates and due years, so this is a separate claim.

**Something to settle when the claim is entered:** this quote does not define AGI. Unless something elsewhere in the same source gives a test, the claim will likely be marked unfalsifiable. That doesn't affect whether it gets in.
